sen.stand: Amounts and deadlines as of: {stand}. Your exact entitlement is decided by the Pflegekasse, your employer or the pension insurance (Rentenversicherung).
sen.antrag.h: Applying for a care level (Pflegegrad): how it works
sen.antrag.lead: One phone call to the Pflegekasse is enough. The Pflegekasse is part of your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse).
sen.antrag.s1.kurz: Call today: money is paid from the month of the application
sen.antrag.s1: Call the Pflegekasse or write a short letter: “Ich beantrage Leistungen der Pflegeversicherung.” (I am applying for long-term care insurance benefits.) Nothing more is needed. The Pflegekasse pays from the month in which you apply, not from the day of the decision. So do not wait until you have all the documents. Write down the date of your call.
sen.antrag.s1.wer: Relatives may call if the person in need of care agrees. A power of attorney (Vollmacht) makes everything easier.
sen.antrag.s2.kurz: Free care advice: appointment within {tage} days
sen.antrag.s2: After the application, the Pflegekasse must offer you free care advice straight away: either a fixed appointment within {tage} days or a voucher for an advice centre that you can use within {tage} days. If you wish, the advisor comes to your home. They help with the application and with planning the help. Advice is also available at the care advice centre (Pflegestützpunkt).
sen.antrag.s3.kurz: Prepare for the assessment: keep a care diary for 1 to 2 weeks
sen.antrag.s3: An assessor usually comes to the home and checks how independent the person is in everyday life. Beforehand, write down for 1 to 2 weeks what the person needs help with and for how long: washing, dressing, eating, walking, medication, at night, when they are restless or confused. Small things count too.
sen.antrag.s4.kurz: At the appointment: honestly show what everyday life is really like
sen.antrag.s4: Many people pull themselves together at the appointment and seem fitter than usual. This can lead to a care level that is too low. Talk about the bad days. Someone who often helps should be there.
sen.antrag.liste.h: Have this ready for the appointment
sen.antrag.liste.3: Aids, for example walker, glasses, hearing aid, incontinence products
sen.antrag.liste.5: Name of the home care service, if one comes
sen.antrag.s5.kurz: Decision: at the latest after {tage} working days
sen.antrag.s5: As a rule, the Pflegekasse must decide in writing within {tage} working days after the application. If it does not manage this and it is the Pflegekasse’s fault, it pays an extra {betrag} for every week that has begun. This does not apply if the person already lives in a care home and already has at least care level 2. If the Pflegekasse asks you for more documents, the deadline only continues once they have arrived there. The assessment must happen faster if the person is in hospital, in rehabilitation or in a hospice, receives palliative care at home, or if you have announced care leave (Pflegezeit) or family care leave (Familienpflegezeit) to your employer. Tell the Pflegekasse this right away when you apply.
sen.antrag.s6.kurz: Do not agree? Objection within 1 month
sen.antrag.s6: If the care level is too low, you can lodge an objection (Widerspruch): in writing to the Pflegekasse, within 1 month. The month counts from the fourth day after the Pflegekasse posted the decision. If it arrives later, the later day counts. The assessment report usually comes together with the decision. If it is missing, request it from the Pflegekasse. Read it carefully and write down what is missing or wrong. Help is available from care advice and from social welfare associations (Sozialverbände).
sen.antrag.s7.kurz: Got worse later? Apply for a higher care level
sen.antrag.s7: If more care is needed, you can apply for a higher care level at any time. It works exactly like the first application.
sen.ang.lead: Caring is a lot of work. There is money, replacement care and protection for you. The most important things first:
sen.ang.top1.kurz: No care level yet? Apply today
sen.ang.top1: Almost all help depends on the care level. Money is only paid from the month of the application. One phone call to the Pflegekasse is enough.
sen.ang.top2: The care advice of the Pflegekasse and the care advice centres (Pflegestützpunkte) help free of charge with the application and with planning. If you wish, the advisor comes to your home.
sen.ang.top3.kurz: Breaks are allowed: the Pflegekasse pays for a replacement
sen.ang.top3: From care level 2, the Pflegekasse pays for a replacement if you go on holiday, are ill or need a few hours for yourself: up to {betrag} a year.
sen.ang.verh.kurz: Replacement care, also by the hour: up to {betrag} a year
sen.ang.verh: From care level 2, respite care and short-term care (Verhinderungspflege and Kurzzeitpflege) share a joint budget of up to {betrag} a year. This also works by the hour, for example one afternoon a week. No money is paid into your account: the Pflegekasse reimburses the costs of the replacement. If close relatives or people from your household step in, there is usually less. Keep the bills: you can also apply for reimbursement afterwards, at the latest by the end of the following calendar year.
sen.ang.fed.kurz: Care by the hour, for example by a family relief service (Familienentlastender Dienst)
sen.ang.fed: Family relief services (Familienentlastende Dienste) and other recognised providers offer care by the hour, accompany people or help in the household. This can be paid for through respite care (Verhinderungspflege) or through the relief amount (Entlastungsbetrag, up to {ent} a month, from care level 1). Ask the provider whether it is recognised for this.
sen.ang.tages.kurz: Day care: well looked after during the day, in addition to the Pflegegeld
sen.ang.tages: In day care (Tagespflege), the person spends the day in a facility; the journey there is included. From care level 2, the Pflegekasse pays for this in addition, up to a fixed monthly amount, and the Pflegegeld is not reduced. You pay for food and accommodation yourself; the relief amount (Entlastungsbetrag) helps with this.
sen.ang.kurs.kurz: Free care courses, also at home
sen.ang.kurs: Care courses show, for example, how to lift and position someone correctly and how to deal with dementia. They are free, even without a care level, and if you wish also at your home. Ask the Pflegekasse.
sen.ang.hilfs.kurz: Care box: gloves and similar items up to {betrag} a month
sen.ang.hilfs: Disposable gloves, disinfectant and bed protection are available from care level 1 up to {betrag} a month, usually as a delivery. A care bed is usually provided on loan.
sen.ang.notruf: If the person is often alone and cannot get help themselves in an emergency, the Pflegekasse can subsidise a home emergency call system (Hausnotruf). Apply to the Pflegekasse beforehand.
sen.ang.umbau.kurz: Adapting the home: up to {betrag} per measure
sen.ang.umbau: For a level-access shower, grab bars or a stairlift there is up to {betrag} per measure. Important: apply before the conversion, with a cost estimate.
sen.ang.akut.kurz: A relative suddenly needs care? Up to {tage} working days off, often with money
sen.ang.akut: If you suddenly have to organise care for a close relative, you may stay away from work for up to {tage} working days, in every company. Tell your employer immediately. If your employer does not pay wages during this time, the Pflegekasse of the person being cared for pays care support allowance (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld), as a rule {prozent} % of the lost net pay. This is paid for at most {tage} working days per calendar year per person in need of care, for all relatives together. Apply to the Pflegekasse immediately. For this you need a certificate from a doctor or a nursing professional.
sen.ang.pzeit.kurz: Care leave (Pflegezeit): up to {monate} months fully or partly off work
sen.ang.pzeit: In companies with more than {beschaeftigte} employees, you can be released from work fully or partly for up to {monate} months to care for a close relative at home. You must announce this at the latest {ankuendigung} working days in advance in text form, for example by letter or e-mail. For accompanying someone in the last phase of life there are up to {letzte} months. In smaller companies you can apply for an agreement; the employer must reply within 4 weeks.
sen.ang.fpz.kurz: Family care leave (Familienpflegezeit): work less for up to {monate} months
sen.ang.fpz: In companies with more than {beschaeftigte} employees (trainees do not count), you can work less for up to {monate} months, but at least {stunden} hours a week. As a rule, you must announce this at the latest {wochen} weeks in advance in text form. Care leave and family care leave together last at most {monate} months. For part of the lost pay, you can apply for an interest-free loan from the Federal Office of Family Affairs and Civil Society Functions (Bundesamt für Familie und zivilgesellschaftliche Aufgaben), also during care leave. You have to pay the loan back.
sen.ang.rente: If you care without pay for at least {stunden} hours a week, spread over at least {tage} days, for someone with care level 2 to 5, and you do not work more than {arbeit} hours a week, the Pflegekasse pays pension contributions for you. This increases your pension. Register with the Pflegekasse as a carer (Pflegeperson).
sen.ang.rente.alt: If you already receive a full old-age pension and have reached the standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze), the Pflegekasse does not pay pension contributions for you. A way out: you choose a partial pension (Teilrente) from the pension insurance, for example 99.99 % of your pension. Then the Pflegekasse pays contributions again, and your pension can still go up. A partial pension can affect a company pension. Get advice from the pension insurance beforehand and inform the Pflegekasse afterwards.
sen.ang.unfall.kurz: Accident insurance while caring, free of charge
sen.ang.unfall: If you care without pay for at least {stunden} hours a week on at least {tage} days for someone with care level 2 to 5, you are covered by statutory accident insurance while caring, for example if you fall while lifting. This also applies if you work full-time. It costs nothing. The responsible body is the accident insurance institution of the municipalities, usually the Unfallkasse.
sen.ang.alv: If you stop working to care for someone, the Pflegekasse can pay contributions to unemployment insurance. Conditions: you care for at least {stunden} hours a week on at least {tage} days for someone with care level 2 to 5, and you were insured directly before or received unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld). If you are still insured through a job, that stays as it is. Ask the Pflegekasse.
sen.ang.pausch.kurz: Tax: carer’s lump sum (Pflege-Pauschbetrag) up to {betrag} a year
sen.ang.pausch: If you care for someone without pay in their home or yours, you can claim the carer’s lump sum (Pflege-Pauschbetrag) in your tax return: for care level 2 {pg2}, for care level 3 {pg3}, for care level 4 and 5 {pg4} a year.
sen.ang.hilfe.kasse: Pflegekasse: the number is on your health insurance card or on the health insurance fund’s website.
sen.ang.hilfe.stp: Care advice centre (Pflegestützpunkt): free advice near you. Ask the Pflegekasse or the town hall for the Pflegestützpunkt for where you live.
sen.ang.hilfe.bmg: Citizens’ hotline of the Federal Ministry of Health on long-term care insurance (general questions, no decisions on individual cases)
sen.selbst.lead: These are the kinds of help that people who receive a pension or are fully unable to work (volle Erwerbsminderung) get most often. The benefits check shows what suits you.
sen.selbst.pflege: Pflegegeld, home care service and relief if you need help in everyday life
sen.selbst.gsa: If your pension is not enough: basic income support in old age and for reduced earning capacity (Grundsicherung im Alter und bei Erwerbsminderung)
sen.selbst.wohngeld: Housing allowance (Wohngeld) if your pension is just above Grundsicherung
sen.selbst.hzp: If care costs more than the Pflegekasse pays
sen.selbst.ausweis: Severe disability card (Schwerbehindertenausweis): compensations for disadvantages, for example free travel or parking concessions
sen.selbst.zuzahl: Limit co-payments at the health insurance fund
sen.selbst.emrente: Pension for reduced earning capacity (Erwerbsminderungsrente) if you can no longer work
sen.selbst.srente: Retiring earlier with a severe disability
